subject: Physics
topicDescription: Distinguishing quantities with magnitude only from those with direction.

sections.heading: Scalars
sections.body: A scalar quantity has magnitude (size) only. Examples include distance, speed, mass, time, and temperature. A scalar can be described with a number and unit, such as a journey of 4 km or a time of 20 s.

sections.heading: Vectors
sections.body: A vector quantity has both magnitude and direction. Examples include displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, and weight. Distance measures the path travelled, while displacement is the straight-line change in position in a stated direction. When vectors act along one line, choose a positive direction and combine them with signs.

keyTerms.definition: A quantity described by magnitude only.
A quantity described by magnitude and direction.
Change in position in a specified direction.

questions.explanation: Velocity has magnitude and direction, so it is a vector.

questions.prompt: What extra information does a vector include compared with a scalar?
questions.explanation: A vector is described by both magnitude and direction; a scalar has magnitude only.
